nodes.title: Provenance staleness: record effective-parent versions per output version, traversing through process nodes
nodes.summary: In a provenance/lineage graph, don't decide staleness per edge (edge.source_version refreshed when the target is saved). When a pipeline has several outputs and only one is regenerated, the refresh of the pipeline's input edges silently marks the siblings fresh. Instead each saved version of a data node records the versions of its effective parents: direct sources plus, through process nodes (pipeline/step/script), the inputs of the process that made it.
nodes.detail: Rules that worked in Sciweave: data node stale if any effective parent's current version != recorded one, or a data parent is itself stale; process nodes are never 'rebuilt', they are flagged 're-run needed' when any of their outputs recorded an older input version; article placements compare placed version vs final/current; informational links (documents/related) never propagate. On new links, setdefault the current versions into the target's latest version (or into all outputs of a process target). A 'cosmetic save' copies the previous version's parents so a font-only re-render stays stale.

nodes.title: Headless Chrome enforces a ~500px minimum window width, so narrow --window-size screenshots show fake overflow
nodes.summary: A --window-size=420,... headless screenshot lays the page out at Chrome's minimum width (~500px) and crops it, so a responsive page looks cut off on the right even when it fits. Verify phone layouts at >=500px or with real device emulation (DevTools / Puppeteer setViewport) before 'fixing' overflow that isn't there.
nodes.trigger: checking a page's mobile/phone layout with headless Chrome or Edge --screenshot at a width under ~500px

nodes.title: Reconstruct a project's analysis history from two independent sources in parallel: files on disk and Claude session transcripts
nodes.summary: To rebuild what was done in a long analysis project, run two read-only agents at once: one mines the folder (README tracker logs, config snapshots, QC reports, file mtimes), the other mines ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl transcripts (condensed to user+assistant text). They cover different things: the file scan gives the canonical outputs, parameters and article mapping; the transcripts give pre-folder work (e.g. months-earlier legacy runs), dead ends, and dated bug fixes that left no file. Merge them into one tree with a fixed output shape ([id] title (dates) · status / summary / params / paths / feeds / history).
nodes.detail: Ask both agents for the same indented markdown schema so it can be parsed mechanically into an import JSON; refer between entries by stable keys (@key) rather than position numbers, since merging reorders the tree.

nodes.title: Same reference-panel file name across tools does not mean same content: compare bytes before merging
nodes.summary: In the SLE project, FIZI (ssimpsmake/resources/refpanel/g1000_eur.bed, 2.86 GB) and LYNXgwas (refpanels/eur/g1000_eur.bed, 1.25 GB) share file names but are different panels, while LYNXgwas refpanels/{eur,eas,amr} are bit-identical to mrmegask ref_panels/suprefpanels/{eur,eas,amr}. Deduplicating or documenting 'which panel was used' by name would have merged the wrong pair and missed the right one.
nodes.detail: Match by size first (free), then SHA-256 only equal-size files; record one node per identical file set with also_at locations and used_by tools. Implemented as sciweave dedup (scan / check / merge) and enforced in plan check.
nodes.trigger: recording or reusing reference panels / annotation files that appear in several pipelines' folders, or deciding two tools 'used the same panel'

nodes.title: On Windows, atomic save via os.replace fails (WinError 5) while another thread/process has the file open: retry briefly
nodes.summary: A local dashboard server re-reads graph.json constantly; a background job saving it with write-temp + os.replace intermittently failed with PermissionError [WinError 5] Access is denied (about 1 in 4 stress runs). POSIX allows replacing an open file, Windows does not. Wrap the replace, the .bak copy and the read in a short retry loop (e.g. 40 x 50 ms), and give each writer its own temp file name (pid + thread id) so concurrent saves never share one.
nodes.detail: Same session: a job registry dict read by polling requests while worker threads add/update jobs raised 'dictionary changed size during iteration' -- guard adds/updates with a lock and iterate over a snapshot copy.
nodes.domain: python / Windows file I/O / threaded local servers
nodes.trigger: writing a file with temp + os.replace on Windows while a server or another process may be reading it, or iterating a shared dict that background threads modify

nodes.title: A pipeline's own output may not be what the next analysis read: hash-match the downstream tool's actual inputs before recording provenance
nodes.summary: gwassnakemake's per-cohort sumstats (PLINK columns) were not what the meta-analysis consumed; post-hoc utility scripts reformatted them (added EAF, catalog columns) and lifted one cohort GRCh38->GRCh37. Only a SHA-256 match against mrmegask/input revealed which files were really used.
nodes.detail: Before recording 'pipeline produces result used by step N', open step N's config, find the exact input paths, and hash-compare them to the candidate files. Converter scripts in a utilities/ folder are part of the provenance chain even if they are kept out of the published pipeline repo.
nodes.trigger: recording which pipeline outputs fed a later analysis, or backing up 'the results that were used'

nodes.title: SMB shares on Windows throw transient OSError [Errno 22] Invalid argument mid-read: retry and resume at the byte offset instead of failing a long copy
nodes.summary: A 13 GB copy from a \\server share died 128 MiB into one file with Errno 22; the same file read fine seconds later. Fix: reopen source, seek to last written byte, truncate dest there, retry with backoff (2/4/8/16 s); keep already-verified files of an interrupted folder copy (same size+mtime) instead of restarting.
nodes.trigger: writing long-running copy/hash code that reads from network shares, especially with parallel heavy reads

nodes.title: Windows PowerShell 5.1 Get-Content -Raw | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 silently corrupts BOM-less UTF-8 source files
nodes.summary: Reading a UTF-8 file without BOM in PS 5.1 decodes it as the ANSI codepage (cp1252), so every non-ASCII char (·, ↑, —) becomes mojibake; Set-Content -Encoding utf8 then writes a BOM and CRLF. The file still passes a JS syntax check, so the damage is easy to miss.
nodes.detail:
Never round-trip source files through Get-Content/Set-Content in PowerShell 5.1; edit with a proper editor tool or Python (open(..., encoding='utf-8', newline='
')). Repair: strip BOM, CRLF->LF, then re-encode each char to cp1252 bytes (code points <256 that cp1252 leaves undefined map to the same byte) and decode as UTF-8; check the git diff shrinks back to the intended edits.
nodes.trigger: doing a quick find/replace on a source file from PowerShell 5.1

nodes.title: Parallel copy jobs that pick 'unique' destination names from already-recorded copies silently overwrite each other
nodes.summary: SciWeave named a copy <id>_<file> only if the plain name was already recorded for another object. Two parallel jobs for files with the same basename (5 runs' metal.simple.tsv.gz) both saw the name free, wrote the same path, and all reported 'ok' while only one file existed. Fix: derive uniqueness from every object that WILL land in the folder (deterministic), refuse a path recorded for another object at record time, and surface a 'conflict' state for shared paths.
nodes.trigger: designing any parallel copy/export where destination names are de-duplicated

nodes.title: Verify an article's printed statistics against the result files before recording provenance
nodes.summary: Before recording which meta-analysis outputs an article used, read every Best-SNP P/OR from the final tables (all sheets), look each SNP up in every candidate result file (main runs, targeted reruns, refits), compare P on log10 within rounding and OR after aligning MR-MEGA's effect allele to METAL's, and list anything matched only by a rerun or not at all. Turned up which numbers came from reruns/refits and that the 9-cohort run survived only as one curated copy.

nodes.title: Two copies of the same GWAS sumstats can differ only in a swapped effect/other allele header: verify with known risk alleles and EAF, never by row values alone
nodes.summary: ssimpsmake's Bentham and Julia files were byte-for-byte the same numbers as the meta-analysis inputs but with effect_allele/other_allele header labels swapped (an older copy). Known SLE risk alleles (STAT4 rs7574865-T, IRF5 rs10488631-C) showed which labelling makes beta point the right way; the EAF column, meanwhile, belonged to the other allele (Bentham rs7574865 EAF 0.77 = G). Consequences: FIZI-imputed Z sign-flipped for those cohorts, and MR-MEGA axes distorted (Bentham+Julia alone at PC0=0.44 vs FIN -0.13), since harmonisation never checked EAF against the panel.
nodes.trigger: the same external summary statistics are used by several pipelines, or MR-MEGA ancestry axes put same-ancestry cohorts far apart

nodes.title: `python -m <pkg>` subprocesses import a same-named folder in the caller's working directory instead of the installed package
nodes.summary: SciWeave's detached copy jobs ran `python -m sciweave` with the caller's cwd; launched from a parent folder containing the 'sciweave' repo checkout, Python imported that folder as a namespace package and every job died (ImportError: cannot import name '__version__' ... unknown location). Fix: set cwd to a neutral/project directory in Popen.
nodes.trigger: spawning `python -m yourpackage` from code that may run in arbitrary directories

nodes.title: Script-safe '</' escaping breaks JS regex literals like /</g
nodes.summary: When inlining JS into HTML, escaping '</' as '</' (to avoid closing the script tag) turns a regex literal such as .replace(/</g, ...) into /</g, a syntax error that silently kills the whole page. Write it as /[<]/g.
nodes.trigger: Inlining a JS file into an HTML page through a function that rewrites '</'

nodes.title: Syntax-highlighted textarea: transparent textarea over a <pre> with identical metrics
nodes.summary: Lightweight code editor without a library: a highlighted <pre> under a transparent-text textarea (caret-color visible), same font/padding/white-space pre-wrap; force overflow-y: scroll on BOTH layers so scrollbar width is equal and soft-wraps line up; sync scrollTop on scroll; line numbers via ::before on per-line divs in the padding gutter.
